children: A cryptocurrency exchange founded by the billionaire Reform UK donor Ben Delo is being sued for £20m over claims that the company mis-sold financial products in the UK. Lewis Barber, who is a software engineer, alleges that BitMEX offered crypto derivative products to investors in the UK, despite not being regulated or approved to do so by the Financial Conduct Authority

Britain will miss out on thousands of jobs and almost £11bn in tax if ministers block the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields, researchers have claimed. A study commissioned by Adura, the energy company behind the two projects, concluded that the Treasury would miss out on £10.9bn of revenue by 2049-50 if the Government did not approve drilling. – Telegraph

An AI company blamed for a 14-year-old’s suicide has filed for bankruptcy. Character.AI, which allowed users to speak to AI avatars with names such as “school bully” or “bad boy best friend”, warned its app could be shut down if no rescue bidder emerged. Founded by former Google engineers, Character.AI was one of the first breakout successes of the ChatGPT era. It soared to a valuation of $2.5bn (£1.9bn), raising nearly $200m. Its app still has an estimated 20 million users, who can create and talk to AI-powered characters. – Telegraph

Three people have been arrested as part of a joint investigation by the City regulator and the police into a suspected organised crime ring involved in insider trading and money laundering. More than 100 staff from the Financial Conduct Authority
were involved in raids of five residential premises in London and Manchester on Tuesday. – The Times
